unit: Unit 12: Everyday Life with Your Computer
title: Online Shopping and Banking
drDigitalIntro:
In Unit 10 you learned how to spot safe websites — now put those skills to use for real shopping and banking.

For online banking:
1. Open your browser and type your bank's address yourself — never click a link in an email or text.
2. Look for the padlock icon and 'https://' at the start of the address before you log in.
3. Sign in with your username and password. If your bank offers two-step verification, turn it on.
4. When you are done, click Log Out — do not just close the tab.
5. Avoid banking on public WiFi (coffee shops, airports) unless you are using a trusted VPN.

For online shopping:
1. Search for the shop you want and look for the padlock before entering card details.
2. Prefer paying by card or through a payment service rather than bank transfer.
3. Keep your order confirmation email — it is proof of purchase if anything goes wrong.
4. If a deal looks too good to be true, search the shop's name plus the word 'reviews' before buying.

Golden rule: when in doubt, type the address yourself — never follow a link you did not ask for.
drDigitalSuccess: You know how to shop and bank safely online! The padlock, https, and typing the address yourself are your three best defences.
drDigitalHint: The key checks are: type the address yourself, look for the padlock, and log out when done. You covered how to spot fake sites in Unit 10.
